headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty fell for a 6th straight week amid rising crude prices and US Fed concerns.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Volatile crude oil prices weighed heavily on market sentiment.
Concerns over US Fed rate decisions reduced investor risk appetite.
Global market caution increased following widespread economic warnings.
Sustained selling pressure dragged major benchmark indices lower for six consecutive weeks.
whatHappening: SENSEX and NIFTY50 closed down, marking their sixth straight weekly decline.
Maruti Suzuki debuted its S-CNG range and set a target to sell 1 million green vehicles in FY27.
Paytm remained in spotlight among key stock-specific triggers.
Markets monitored developments around Tata Sons and global macroeconomic trends.

summary: On the last trading day, Indian benchmark indices SENSEX and NIFTY50 fell for a sixth straight week amid crude oil price fluctuations and US Fed rate triggers. Global market warnings and institutional selling continued to keep pressure on key heavyweights across sectors. Meanwhile, stock-specific movements were highlighted by Maruti Suzuki's green vehicle announcements and Paytm being in focus.
